visual_grammar.background: full-bleed hypercolor backdrop built from a deep electric-blue to violet radial gradient with blown-out white flash bloom zones, subtle disposable-camera film grain, faint halftone speckle, and occasional neon-yellow sticker shapes tucked into corners; never clean corporate white, always high-energy and flash-burned
visual_grammar.foreground: bright white primary text and keyline treatment with occasional reversed-out black text inside loud sticker bursts; all content must read like toy packaging and captured evidence, not consulting slides
visual_grammar.accent: screaming neon yellow starburst/sticker treatment used consistently for proof callouts, price bursts, and short emphatic labels
visual_grammar.typography: heavy condensed 90s toy-ad sans for headlines in all caps, extra-bold italic sans for short burst phrases, straightforward bold grotesk sans for body copy, narrow monospaced microtype only for tiny caution-style annotations
visual_grammar.diagram_style: simple high-contrast exploded schematics and mechanism arrows with solid white outlines, translucent purple and blue fills, glow edges around energy paths, hand-applied proof stamps, and blunt directional labels rather than technical elegance
visual_grammar.panel_style: cropped photo and info panels as taped-on or stickered evidence blocks with hard flash edges, white or electric-blue borders, slight rotation offsets, and occasional black shadow knockouts; no soft corporate cards
visual_grammar.grid_system: 12-column grid with large outer margins, oversized top-left headline zone, dominant central hero image area, and lower-third band for punchy support copy or callouts; asymmetrical but disciplined packaging-style composition
visual_grammar.line_weight: thick 3-5 px keylines and dividers, chunky arrows, bold stamp outlines, no delicate hairlines

authorized_inferences.pricing: Proposed launch pricing: Voltex starter unit at $129.99 MSRP including one color cartridge, refill noble gas color cartridges at $14.99 each, 3-cartridge chromatic pack at $34.99, and a six-color collector bundle at $179.99. Proposed retail structure assumes the starter drives entry while cartridges supply recurring accessory revenue.
authorized_inferences.mockup_prototype_design: Canonical proposed product mockup for all slides: a bright translucent blue plastic Voltex body with a glowing purple spherical center chamber, long ribbed translucent barrel ending in a wide flared muzzle, a visible orange cartridge bay along the upper rear side, a chunky blue rear grip, and a translucent hot-pink under-bar pump/striker handle. The silhouette is oversized, rounded, and aggressively non-tactical, like handheld science equipment. When shown firing, the emitted plasma bolt is vivid argon purple unless the slide explicitly depicts a cartridge color swap concept; all product depictions must match the supplied reference form factor exactly.

storyboard.title: VOLTEX
storyboard.purpose: Title cover. Establish immediate impossible-to-ignore product identity with one dominant name, one short tagline, and a single hero visual that makes the object feel real, toy-like, and shockingly physical. Speaker notes should frame the opening as: do not start with explanation; start with the object and let the room feel the category rupture first.
storyboard.image_prompt: Create a clean full-bleed digital screenshot of a single presentation slide, exported edge-to-edge with no software UI and absolutely no page number, slide count, or pagination indicator anywhere. This is the deck's one and only cover slide. Layout: huge VOLTEX logotype in the upper left, one short tagline beneath it reading 'IT SHOOTS LIGHTNING.' Keep text minimal and leave generous negative space. Dominant hero visual: the canonical proposed product mockup shown large across the right two-thirds of the slide, angled three-quarters, glowing from within, matching the supplied reference form exactly: bright translucent blue body, purple spherical center chamber, ribbed barrel, wide flared muzzle, visible orange side cartridge bay, hot-pink under-bar pump handle, non-threatening science-equipment silhouette. Add hard flash bloom and subtle evidence-photo energy but keep this slide cleaner than the rest. Include one small neon-yellow sticker burst near the product reading 'REAL PLASMA TOY' as a packaging-style accent. No charts, no diagrams, no extra panels, no people, no claims beyond the tagline and sticker callout.

storyboard.title: LOOK AT WHAT THE CAMERA HAD TO ADMIT
storyboard.purpose: First argumentative slide. Lead with the tactical gap: in a category built on fake spectacle, documented-looking backyard imagery is the advantage. Speaker notes should present Voltex as the rare toy whose most persuasive asset is not rendering but disbelief-provoking photography. Use only mockup/illustrative imagery, not implied real proof.

storyboard.title: WHY IT READS AS A TOY INSTANTLY
storyboard.purpose: Translate form factor into parent and retail legibility. Emphasize that the silhouette, materials, and two-hand interaction are engineering-driven and aggressively non-firearm. Speaker notes should stress that the same constraints that make the physics work also force a safer, more legible play object.

storyboard.title: HOW THE SHOT WORKS
storyboard.purpose: Explain the mechanism simply enough to remove disbelief without drowning the room in physics. Speaker notes should present the sequence as an engineering fact: charge, ignite, confine, release, dissipate. This is Newton-style credibility through calm mechanism, not hype.

storyboard.title: WHY KIDS PUSH IT AND PARENTS ALLOW IT
storyboard.purpose: Show demand logic and the social theater of backyard play, while pairing it with the safety case grounded in mechanism limits. Speaker notes should argue that thrilling and bounded are not opposites here; the same physical limits that constrain the projectile create the purchase rationale.
